newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt extends detention of Israeli spy suspect.
newsitem.headline: Egypt extends detention of Israeli spy suspect.

text.p: Alleged Israeli spy Azam Azam made his first public appearance in an Egyptian court on Monday and was remanded in custody for another 45 days, witnesses said.

Ali Wahbi, the judge presiding over the remand hearing, ordered Azam, 35, out of a courtroom cage to defend himself in an emotional session attended by Israeli embassy officials and relatives, they added.
Wahbi ordered Azam, chief mechanic at an Israeli-owned textile factory in Egypt, to be held for a second 45-day period.
Security authorities arrested Azam in Cairo last month along with Egyptian national Emadeddin Abdel Hamid. Azam has not been formally charged and no date has been set for his trial.
Arriving in the court, he hugged his two brothers and wept. One of the brothers is working in Egypt, security sources said.

"Treatment is good at the prison and the consul is visiting me frequently," Azam told reporters in a brief statement, before he asked them to talk only to his lawyer. The Israeli consul, Shuki Gabai, attended the session.
The prosecutor said in his statement to the court: "This defendant wanted to harm the country which is seeking peace... but they (the Israelis) repaid this with ingratitude."
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel but ties have cooled sharply since right-wing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office in June.

The prosecutor said Azam had facilitated a sexual affair between Abdel Hamid and one of two Israeli-Arab women involved in the case but at large -- Mona Ahmed Shawahna and Zahra Youssef Greiss. Azam himself is of Arab origin.
"He (Abdel Hamid) did not respond to Azam's pressures for the sake of any principle, but in return for lusts, sex and money," he added.
Azam denied the espionage allegations. He said the last time he met Abdel Hamid was in Israel in February.
Among prosecution evidence were clothes described as producing invisible ink when washed.
Israel has insisted Azam is innocent and demands his release. A court earlier this month extended Abdel Hamid's detention for 45 days.
The prosecution was expected to issue the charge sheet a few weeks ago, amid reports that it was waiting for a political decision in the case.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has said Israeli leaders squandered the chance to secure Azam's release through quiet diplomacy by making the affair public.
